sources.entry: FreeScout - Email-based customer support application, help desk and shared mailbox (alternative to Zendesk and Help Scout). (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: FreeScout is a self-hosted, PHP (Laravel) email-based help desk and shared inbox positioned as a free alternative to Zendesk and Help Scout.
summary.what_it_does: FreeScout centralizes customer conversations that arrive by email, and the README also lists WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook, Slack and Live Chat as channels. It supports unlimited agents, tickets and mailboxes, and connects to mail through SMTP, IMAP and POP3, with OAuth sign-in for Microsoft Office 365 and Google Workspace. Agents can share internal notes, forward, merge or move conversations, star or follow them, send auto replies, and see collision warnings when two agents open the same conversation. It includes a web installer and updater, a Progressive Web App with push notifications, native S3 storage support, and powerful search. The README says it is a pure PHP/MySQL application and can run on shared hosting.
use_cases: run a shared support inbox for a small team
manage help desk tickets without a SaaS subscription
route customer messages from multiple mailboxes
how_to_run: Follow the Installation Guide linked in the README
Or use the Docker Image listed in the README
Or use a one-click installer such as Cloudron, Softaculous, or the Ubuntu Bash script
Run the web installer to complete setup
notable: Free alternative to Zendesk and Help Scout, developed from scratch without copyrighted materials from either
Email-first design with SMTP, IMAP and POP3 support plus OAuth for Office 365 and Google Workspace
Installable Progressive Web App with web push notifications and a macOS menu bar app
Modules system with official and community extensions, plus an API and Zapier/Make integrations
Web installer and updater; available in 33 languages
caveats: Requires PHP and a MySQL-compatible or PostgreSQL database; not a single-binary install
Mobile apps support the same modules as the web version, and some modules may be community-maintained
Some README-listed channels and AI features depend on modules or integrations that are not described in detail
